answer: Each settlement leaves a public pigment on the payer and payee keys: a compact hash of counterparties, amounts, and timing. When a payment ripple fans out through the graph, the protocol clusters keys whose traces are statistically interchangeable and treats the cluster as one identity for voting and withdrawal. A farm that spins a fable of many names from one operator cannot multiply influence, because shared counterparties and synchronized timing collapse them back to a single seat, and the clustered stake can be slashed.
